lessons.title: Tax years, accounting methods and records

pool.q: In the accounting equation, what are liabilities and equity?
options: Liabilities are cash; equity is inventory
Liabilities are sales; equity is expenses
Liabilities are what the business owes; equity is the part that belongs to the owner
They are two names for the same thing
pool.explain: Assets = Liabilities + Equity.
pool.evidence: Liabilities are what it owes, and equity is the amount of the company that belongs to the business owner.

pool.q: What are financial statements?
options: Formal reports on a company's financial position, cash inflows and outflows, and results of operations
pool.explain: They include the balance sheet, income statement and statement of cash flows.
pool.evidence: These financial statements are formal reports providing information on a company’s financial position, cash inflows and outflows, and the results of operations.

pool.q: Financial statements used by external entities are prepared using…
pool.explain: Common rules make statements comparable between companies.
pool.evidence: Financial statements used by external entities are prepared using Generally Accepted Accounting Principles

pool.q: Under accrual basis accounting, when are revenue and expenses recorded?
options: When revenue is earned and expenses are incurred, regardless of when payment is received
At the end of the year only
pool.explain: Cash basis records them when payment is received or made.
pool.evidence: Revenue is recorded when it is earned and expenses are recorded when they are incurred, regardless of when payment is received.

pool.q: Why do GAAP require accrual accounting?
options: It gives a more accurate picture of a company's financial condition
It is simpler to calculate than the cash basis
It always reduces the tax bill
It ignores sales made on credit
pool.explain: Matching revenue and expenses to the period they belong to shows true performance.
pool.evidence: GAAP require accrual accounting because it presents a more accurate picture of a company

pool.q: Under cash basis accounting, when is revenue recorded?
options: At the end of the financial year
pool.explain: Expenses likewise are recorded when payment is made — the difference from accrual is timing.
pool.evidence: Revenue is recorded when payment is received and expenses are recorded when payment is made.

pool.q: For tax reporting, who is generally permitted to use the cash basis?
options: Sole proprietors and certain other small businesses
pool.explain: Bigger businesses and corporations are generally required to use the accrual basis.
pool.evidence: Generally, cash basis reporting is permitted for sole proprietors and certain other small businesses.

pool.q: In double-entry bookkeeping, on which side are debits recorded?
options: On the left (credits are on the right)
On the right (credits are on the left)
pool.explain: Every transaction has equal debits and credits.
pool.evidence: debits are on the left and credits are on the right

pool.q: What are accounts?
options: The categories used to track the financial information that is important to us
pool.explain: Examples include Cash, Accounts Receivable, Revenue and Supplies.
pool.evidence: Accounts are the categories that we use to track the financial information that is important to us.

pool.q: What is a journal in bookkeeping?
options: A summary of balances by account
A chronological list of economic events (transactions)
pool.explain: Entries are later posted to the ledger, which sorts them by account.
pool.evidence: it is still a chronological list of economic events (transactions)

pool.q: What does it mean to buy supplies 'on account'?
options: You paid cash on the spot
You received them but have not paid for them yet
You returned them for a refund
You bought them on behalf of a customer
pool.explain: Buying on credit creates a liability (accounts payable) until you pay.
pool.evidence: means that we picked up the items but did not yet pay for them

pool.q: When you pay by cheque, how is the checking (cash) account posted?
options: It is credited, because the cheque reduces it
It is debited, because money was spent
It is not touched until the cheque clears
pool.explain: Cash is an asset: credits decrease assets, debits increase them.
pool.evidence: we are going to post a credit to the checking account, noting that we are reducing that account by the amount of the check written

pool.q: The journal, or book of original entry, is compared to what?
options: An instruction manual for whoever posts the transactions to the ledger
pool.explain: Each journal entry tells the bookkeeper which ledger accounts to debit and credit.
pool.evidence: is like an instruction manual to whoever is going to post these transactions to the ledger

pool.q: How do you run a trial balance?
options: Add up the month's cash receipts
Compare this month's revenue with last month's
List debit balances in one column and credit balances in another, then compare the totals
Count the cash in the till
pool.explain: If the totals match, debits equal credits — though some errors can still hide.
pool.evidence: Put all the debit balances in one column, and all the credit balances in another, and compare the totals

pool.q: When are adjusting journal entries made?
options: At the end of an accounting period, or whenever financial statements are prepared, so revenues and expenses match
Only when there is an error
pool.explain: Adjustments apply the matching principle of accrual accounting.
pool.evidence: adjusting journal entries are made at the end of an accounting period or any time financial statements are prepared so that we have matching revenues and expenses.

pool.q: Revenue has been earned but the customer has not been billed yet. What kind of adjusting entry records it?
pool.explain: The entry records a receivable and the earned revenue in the right period.
pool.evidence: This is a prototypical accrued revenue entry.

pool.q: What does the lesson recommend to catch accounting errors?
options: Routinely run checks and make the necessary adjusting entries
pool.explain: Regular checks keep errors from carrying into the financial statements.
pool.evidence: It is good practice to routinely run checks to catch errors and create the necessary journal adjusting entries.

pool.q: After identifying the type of error, how should you classify it?
options: As a debit or a credit
As an asset or an expense
As a deferral (prepayment) or an accrual
pool.explain: The classification tells you which adjusting entry fixes it.
pool.evidence: time to classify it as a deferral (also known as prepayment) or an accrual

pool.q: Which financial statement is prepared first?
pool.explain: Net income from the income statement feeds into the statements that follow.
pool.evidence: The first statement to prepare is the Income Statement.

pool.q: Why is the report format of the balance sheet more widely used than the account format?
options: Today's complex balance sheets are hard to present side by side
The report format leaves out equity
pool.explain: The report format lists assets, then liabilities, then equity, top to bottom.
pool.evidence: the report format (assets first, then liabilities, and finally the equity, top to bottom) is so much more widely used

pool.q: In the closing process, where are the credit balances of revenue accounts transferred?
options: To a clearing account called Income Summary
pool.explain: Income Summary is then closed to the owner's capital (or retained earnings).
pool.evidence: Closing the revenue accounts: transferring the credit balances in the revenue accounts to a clearing account called Income Summary.

pool.q: Where is a discrepancy in the petty cash fund posted?
options: To an account called Cash Over and Short
pool.explain: Small errors make the cash in the box differ from the fund less the vouchers.
pool.evidence: We post the discrepancy to an account called Cash Over and Short.

pool.q: Why do businesses keep a petty cash fund?
options: It is more convenient than going to accounts payable for every small purchase
pool.explain: Petty cash covers stamps, coffee for meetings and similar small costs.
pool.evidence: Having a petty cash account is just more convenient than going to the accounts payable clerk every time someone needs a stamp

pool.q: If the petty cash fund is closed because it is no longer needed, what is the journal entry?
options: The same as the establishing entry
The reverse of the entry that established the fund
A debit to Cash Over and Short
pool.explain: Returning surplus cash to the bank is recorded the same way.
pool.evidence: the entry is the reverse of the establishing entry

pool.q: Which internal controls does the petty cash system include?
options: Segregation of duties, assignment of responsibility and reconciliation
pool.explain: One responsible person holds the fund, others approve and reconcile it.
pool.evidence: most notably segregation of duties, assignment of responsibility, and a reconciliation (monitoring) process

pool.q: To prevent collusion, who should reconcile the bank account?
options: Someone who is not involved in the cash disbursement cycle
The person who writes the cheques
pool.explain: Ideally the bank also mails the statement directly to that person.
pool.evidence: the person who reconciles the bank account should not be involved in the cash disbursement cycle

pool.q: An item is added on the book side of a bank reconciliation. How is it recorded?
options: As a credit to the checking account
It is not recorded at all
As a debit to an expense account
As a debit to the checking account, since debits increase assets
pool.explain: Items that reconcile the book balance to the adjusted bank balance must be recorded in the general ledger.
pool.evidence: If we added an item in the bank reconciliation, we will DEBIT the checking account (because a debit increases an asset account in a GL).

pool.q: What is net pay?
options: The amount an employee receives after all taxes and voluntary deductions
The salary promised in the contract
pool.explain: Gross pay is the amount promised before deductions.
pool.evidence: Net Pay: This is the amount an employee receives after all taxes and voluntary deductions have been taken out.

pool.q: According to the IRS, what is an accounting method?
options: A set of rules used to determine when and how income and expenses are reported
pool.explain: The two most common are the cash and accrual methods.
pool.evidence: An accounting method is a set of rules used to determine when and how income and expenses are reported.

pool.q: What is a tax year?
options: Any twelve months you choose each year
The annual accounting period on which you figure taxable income
The time you have to pay your tax
pool.explain: Your income tax return is filed based on it.
pool.evidence: You must figure your taxable income and file an income tax return based on an annual accounting period called a tax year.

pool.q: If you need an inventory to account for your income, which method must you generally use for purchases and sales?
pool.explain: Inventory businesses must match purchases and sales to the periods they belong to.
pool.evidence: If an inventory is necessary to account for your income, you must generally use an accrual method of accounting for purchases and sales.

pool.q: What is one of the first things to do when you start a business, for good records?
pool.explain: Separating business and personal money makes records clear and supportable.
pool.evidence: One of the first things you should do when you start a business is open a business checking account.

pool.q: You write a cheque for cash to pay a business expense. What should you keep?
options: The receipt for the cash payment, with your records
Nothing — the cheque stub is enough
A note in your personal diary
pool.explain: Supporting documents prove what each payment was for.
pool.evidence: If you must write a check for cash to pay a business expense, include the receipt for the cash payment in your records.

pool.q: In the recordkeeping example, what does Henry never pay with cheques from the business account?
pool.explain: Keeping business and personal money separate keeps the records clean.
pool.evidence: Henry does not pay personal or nonbusiness expenses by checks drawn on the business account.

pool.q: Why are Henry's business cheques prenumbered?
options: So the bank can sort them faster
Because the tax office issues the numbers
So every cheque number is listed and accounted for
To show which payments matter most
pool.explain: A missing number in the journal is an immediate warning sign.
pool.evidence: All checks are prenumbered and each check number is listed and accounted for in the column provided in the journal.
